fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Landscaped Area; Walkway; Front Entry Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the street in both directions.
• Identify and mark the primary access point clearly so responding units do not commit to a secondary or restricted entry.
• Keep at least one parking area clear of vehicles to provide a staging or turnaround space for emergency equipment.
• Confirm that walkway and front entry paths are kept clear of parked vehicles, lawn equipment, or landscaping debris that could block foot access to the front door.
• Trim any landscaping along the driveway or walkways that narrows the path or reduces visibility for approaching responders.
• Post the physical address number at the front entry in addition to the street-facing sign to help responders confirm they have reached the correct unit.
• If turnaround space is insufficient for larger emergency vehicles, designate and keep clear a specific area where vehicles can reverse or reposition without obstruction.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Trees; Multiple Access Routes; Vegetation Groups
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near the structure to raise the canopy off the ground.
• Keep vegetation groups separated from one another so fire cannot move easily between them toward the structure.
• Clear any dead or dry plant material from within the vegetation groups closest to the structure.
• Maintain open ground between the scattered shrubs and the base of the structure.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim back any shrubs or low branches along the driveway edges that could block a vehicle or reduce visibility.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structure free of new shrub or brush growth.
